title: Circular common-host WASP-105 models at 10 degrees lose retained inner transit bands by 2035
abstract: We test whether an inclined inner planet can keep transiting at all nine TESS sector dates for the WASP-105 candidate. We use 48 Newtonian three-body integrations with circular starting orbits, three inner masses from 1 to 25 Earth masses, two starting phases and eight tilts from 0 to 30 degrees. At a giant impact parameter of 0.17, the 10-degree models retain 41.6 to 42.7 percent of initially visible viewing directions. All retained directions leave the inner transit band at least once before 2035 January 1. At 15 degrees, 7.3 to 7.9 percent remain through the past dates, and all leave the band before 2030. At 20 and 30 degrees no direction passes all dates, with a margin larger than the angular grid error. All directions pass at tilts through 5 degrees and stay in band through 2040. Two integrators and a smaller step support the result. The nodal period near alignment is about 42 years and agrees with linear secular theory within one percent. Changing the giant impact parameter to 0 or 0.5 leaves 97.4 to 100 percent of retained 10-degree directions with loss before 2035. These are viewing fractions under a specified model, not a measured inclination or planet confirmation. Eccentric starting orbits, host ambiguity, weak sector signals and fixed stellar properties limit application to the real system. No flux data are fitted. The package contains original code, all simulated orbits, aggregate results, a figure and exact source date provenance.

display.caption: Viewing selection, transit-band loss before 2035 and nodal periods for circular initial orbits. The giant reference impact parameter is 0.17. Points show zero-phase examples for three inner masses. Lines join tested inclinations; they do not establish a tilt threshold. No retained views exist at 20 or 30 degrees.
